updates.name: Mark Tedesco
updates.bio: Retired U.S. EPA manager who directed the EPA Long Island Sound Office and the Long Island Sound Study (now the Long Island Sound Partnership) from 1996 until April 2025, after about 38 years with EPA, most of them devoted to the Sound's restoration. He was succeeded by Nicole Tachiki as acting director.

updates.name: Martin Tresguerres
updates.bio: Professor in the Marine Biology Research Division at UC San Diego's Scripps Institution of Oceanography; he joined Scripps in 2010 and directed the division from 2018 to 2022. His lab examines acid-base regulation, symbiosis, neurobiology and biomineralization in phytoplankton, corals and fish, and he leads the Allen Discovery Center on neurobiology in changing environments (ADC-NiCE).
updates.research_interests: physiology of aquatic organisms; pH, CO2 and bicarbonate sensing; cell signaling; ion transport and acid/base regulation; epithelial physiology; aquatic symbioses; biomineralization

Her recent publications centre on long-term experiments at West Virginia's Fernow Experimental Forest, including whole-watershed acidification, nitrogen additions, soil productivity and fertility, and stand development on gauged watersheds.

updates.name: Matthew J. Rinella
updates.bio: Rangeland management specialist with USDA-ARS at the Fort Keogh Livestock and Range Research Laboratory, Miles City, Montana, trained in weed science and community ecology (Ph.D., Montana State). He investigates how invaded rangeland plant communities respond to grazing, herbicides, seeding and biocontrol, and how to forecast and prevent new invasions, using field experiments and quantitative models.
updates.research_interests: rangeland invasive plant ecology; predicting invaded-community responses to grazing, biocontrol, seeding and herbicides; preventing plant invasions; habitat susceptibility to invasion; leafy spurge and spotted knapweed competition; quantitative ecological modeling
updates.current_affiliation: USDA-ARS Fort Keogh Livestock and Range Research Laboratory, Miles City, MT

updates.name: Megan N. Dethier
updates.bio: Marine intertidal ecologist and University of Washington research professor based at Friday Harbor Laboratories, which she currently directs. Her work covers plant-herbivore interactions, classification and long-term monitoring of intertidal and nearshore habitats and their biodiversity, effects of shoreline armoring, and invertebrate functional morphology.
updates.research_interests: marine intertidal ecology; plant-herbivore interactions; classification and long-term monitoring of intertidal habitats; maintenance of intertidal biodiversity; nearshore habitat monitoring; shoreline armoring; invertebrate functional morphology

updates.name: Merryl Alber
updates.bio: Professor of marine sciences at the University of Georgia who directs its Sapelo Island-based Marine Institute; she is lead principal investigator of the Georgia Coastal Ecosystems LTER. Her research addresses nearshore and estuarine ecology, including salt-marsh change, estuarine food webs and flushing, freshwater withdrawal effects, and links between coastal science and policy.

updates.name: Michael L. Pace
updates.bio: Aquatic ecosystem ecologist, now emeritus W.W. Corcoran Professor of Natural History at UVA, after earlier posts at McGill, the University of Hawaii and the Cary Institute. He studies how aquatic ecosystems are structured and function and respond to environmental change, notably resilience and regime shifts tested through whole-lake manipulations; ASLO Hutchinson and Redfield awardee.
updates.research_interests: structure and function of aquatic ecosystems; causes and consequences of environmental change; resilience and state change in aquatic ecosystems; whole-lake manipulation experiments

Earlier roles include executive director of the National Science Board, NOAA senior advisor for international science policy, and NOAA chief scientist for national marine sanctuaries and estuarine research reserves; his work emphasizes moving science into policy and practice.
